entries.key: [Ends the match when the model reaches the selected confidence. Spectators can see the predicted win chances in statistics.]
entries.source: Ends the match when the model reaches the selected confidence. Spectators can see the predicted win chances in statistics.
Each colony's figures for the whole match. The highest is highlighted where more is better; click a column heading to see how it changed over time.
How many units the colony had alive: workers, explorers and warriors together.
How fast swarms were producing new units. Split it to see workers, explorers and warriors separately.
How fast the colony was losing units, whatever the cause: combat, starvation, injuries while clearing, or being trapped.
Units born minus units lost. Above zero the colony was growing; below zero it was shrinking.
What the colony's units died of: fighting, starvation, injuries while clearing resources, being trapped with no way out, or other causes.
Units won over from other colonies minus units lost to them. Units change sides when another colony feeds them better.

How much food the colony's units were carrying inside them. Each unit is placed by how much of its food reserve is left: nearly empty (a quarter or less), low (up to half), half full (up to three quarters) or well fed. Units go looking for an inn as their reserve runs down, so a colony always has some that are low.
How healthy the colony's units were. Each unit is placed by how many of its hit points are left: critical (a quarter or less), wounded (up to half), hurt (up to three quarters) or healthy.
Units that had stopped work to find an inn. Those that are also below full health are counted as weakening.
Units inside an inn eating or inside a hospital being healed, and so not working.
Loads of food harvested by workers from food-producing resources. Inns turn food into meals.
Food sitting in the colony's buildings, ready to be served or used.
Meals the colony's inns served, to its own units and to visitors from other colonies.
Units that died because they could not find food in time.
Hit points the colony's hospitals gave back to wounded units.
Loads of every material harvested by workers. Split it to see each material.
Materials sitting in the colony's buildings. Split it to see each material.
Where delivered materials went: meals, new units, tower ammunition, new buildings or upgrades.
Materials received through markets minus materials given away.
Building work completed: new buildings, upgrades and repairs.
A score for the combined fighting power of the colony's warriors: how hard and how fast they hit.
A score for the combined firepower of the colony's defence towers.
The hit points of all the colony's units and buildings added together.
Damage the colony did to enemy units and buildings. Split it to see warriors, magic and towers.
Damage enemies did to the colony's units and buildings.
Damage dealt minus damage taken. Above zero the colony was winning its fights.
